items.text: a king in all but name?
Idus Martiae: the Ides of March

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who stabbed Julius Caesar 23 times?
beats.say: Who stabbed Julius Caesar twenty-three times?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: His own senators. On the fifteenth of March, 44 BC, the day Romans called the Ides.
beats.say: His own senators. On the fifteenth of March, forty-four BC, the day Romans called the Ides.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where did it happen?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In a meeting hall built by Pompey. Its ruins lie in a square in central Rome, now home to a sanctuary for hundreds of cats.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why kill him?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A few weeks earlier, Caesar had been named dictator for life. Many senators feared he would make himself king.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who was behind it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: More than sixty men, led by Brutus and Cassius. Caesar had pardoned Brutus after the civil war and treated him almost like a son.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Was he warned?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Twice. A seer named Spurinna warned him of danger by the Ides. And his wife Calpurnia dreamed of his death and begged him to stay home.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: On the way, Caesar joked: the Ides of March have come. Spurinna replied: yes, but they have not gone.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: What happened inside?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The senators surrounded him and pulled out daggers hidden in their togas. He fell at the foot of a statue of Pompey, his old rival.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Twenty-three wounds?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Yes. A doctor named Antistius examined the body. Only one wound, the second, was fatal. It's the first autopsy in recorded history.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Did he really say: Et tu, Brute?
beats.say: Did he really say: Et too, Brootay?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: No, that line comes from Shakespeare. One Roman writer says Caesar died in silence. Others say his last words were, in Greek: you too, child?

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Did the killers win?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Brutus even minted coins with two daggers and the words EID MAR, the Ides of March. But in 42 BC, Caesar's heir Octavian and Mark Antony defeated them at Philippi, and Brutus and Cassius took their own lives.
beats.say: Brutus even minted coins with two daggers and the words: eed mar, the Ides of March. But in forty-two BC, Caesar's heir Octavian and Mark Antony defeated them at Philippi, and Brutus and Cassius took their own lives.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So is Caesar forgotten?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Far from it. The month of July is named after him, and his name became the word for emperor: Kaiser in German, Tsar in Russian.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Next time: Octavian becomes Augustus, the first emperor. Like the video and follow History Sketches so you don't miss it.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments: was Brutus a hero or a traitor?
